research_updates.title: Boundary and operating chronology verified
research_updates.notes: IM3 record 00626785488 is one 654,433-square-foot mapped footprint within a multi-building Los Lunas campus and supplies no building name or public-record crosswalk. State and Village records date the first campus groundbreaking to October 2016, the first online building to 2017, a campus grand opening to February 7, 2019, and six online buildings to 2022; Meta's current factsheet separately labels the data center online in 2018. The SEC subsidiary list ties Greater Kudu LLC to Facebook, but none of these records identifies which chronology or legal subaccount belongs to the selected footprint. The later 2021 two-building expansion, subsequent expansion load, the 2025 AI expansion, tenant equipment, off-site renewable projects and other Meta facilities remain outside the selected-building boundary.

source.notes: The selected inventory object is IM3 building record 00626785488, a 654,433-square-foot mapped footprint at 34.830246608460115, -106.78382909936067. IM3 separately maps four other buildings and a campus polygon at the Los Lunas site; the record does not provide a building name, construction cost, opening date, parcel, permit or utility-account crosswalk.

research_updates.title: Original incentive authorization is not realized value
research_updates.notes: The June 23, 2016 bond package and Ordinance 407 were reviewed for original-project terms. Authorization for as many as six $5 billion industrial-revenue-bond series is a financing ceiling, not issued principal, capital expenditure, tax abatement, cash grant, property-tax saving or public cost. Later 2021 and 2025 bond packages concern expansions and are excluded. No selected-building bond draw, lease payment or realized incentive value was located.

source.title: Village Council agenda package, June 23, 2016, Ordinance 407
source.notes: The original Greater Kudu industrial-revenue-bond package authorizes up to six series of as much as $5 billion each for construction and equipping of the data-center campus. Those maximum principal amounts are legal authorization ceilings, not issued debt, expenditure, capital investment, subsidy or realized tax benefit.

research_updates.title: Campus parcel is fully exempt in the 2023 assessor revision
research_updates.notes: The County assessor's exact-address result resolves to Village-owned UPC 1006040261023 / account R302913, a 738.15-acre campus parcel with business name FACEBOOK. The 2023 County fields report $19,930,050 actual value, $6,643,350 total assessed value, an equal other exemption and zero net assessed value. Those stocks are retained at unallocated campus scope; they are not a cash estimate of tax savings. Village FY2017-FY2023 GASB 77 schedules separately mark the Greater Kudu agreement under construction and PILOT receipts N/A for the school district, State and County. The report's unrelated $450,000 Village-wide PILOT total is excluded, and no selected-building or personal-property account, bill, payment, taxing-jurisdiction receipt, lease revenue, service cost or net fiscal result was found.

source.title: Valencia County parcel record for 4250 Messenger Loop NW
source.notes: The County's live ArcGIS parcel service resolves the exact campus address to UPC 1006040261023 and account R302913, a 738.15-acre parcel owned by the Village of Los Lunas with business name FACEBOOK. Revision-year 2023 fields report $19,930,050 actual value, $6,643,350 total assessed value, an equal $6,643,350 other exemption, and zero net assessed value. research_updates.title: Public-cost search supports fund flows with scope limits
research_updates.notes: Village budgets from FY2017 through FY2025, Resolution 16-26, the 2016 development agreements, the 2021 PPA amendment and dedicated infrastructure accounts were searched for State LEDA, Local LEDA GRT, Facebook, Greater Kudu and Meta flows. The original formula dedicated 75% of specified Village gross-receipts-tax distributions attributable to construction, and the development minutes state that no impact fees applied, but no realized waiver value was disclosed. Actual State LEDA receipts total $10 million across FY2017-FY2018; FY2021 actual outlays are $2,043,636 in the State project fund and $1,130,805 in the local fund. The FY2024 NM 6 traffic account separately reports $529,277 of revenue and $23,200 of capital purchases, and Village records identify Meta as payer for the completed off-site system. Receipts and expenditures are separate flows and are not summed or netted. The 2021 amendment says Greater Kudu declined some reimbursements and the Village would contract directly for revised infrastructure, but gives no dollar reconciliation. None of these funds is an IM3-building allocation or a complete marginal public-cost account.

source.title: Village of Los Lunas FY2022 Final Budget
source.notes: The budget reports FY2021 actual expenditures for both the State LEDA Facebook Project Fund and the Local LEDA GRT Fund. The local fund receives transfers tied to project-attributable gross-receipts-tax distributions but finances water-system and rail-park projects with wider service areas.

research_updates.title: Permit, planning, construction and fire searches lack an IM3 crosswalk
research_updates.notes: The Village planning and zoning agenda archive, development-plan and permit page, fire-prevention and public-works access points, and state Construction Industries Division portal were searched for 2016-2026. The exact campus address returned 20 state records: 11 electrical, five mechanical, three general-construction and one modular record, with 13 closed and seven issued statuses. Their 2021-2026 labels use VCN, VLL6, later halls, administrative or temporary work; one detail page records a passed 2024 security final inspection, but no record supplies an IM3 crosswalk, permit fee or certificate of occupancy. An exact portal search for legacy record ELEC_2017005671, cited by a secondary aggregator as a 108-MW data-center permit, returned no record, so the secondary fee claim was not retained. No selected-building permit valuation, fee, inspection, construction start or contractor-payment value can be established, and post-2020 work is not used as original-building evidence. Complete applications, approved plans, fee receipts, inspection histories and certificates remain records-request targets for CID and the Village.

source.title: New Mexico public permit search
source.publisher: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department, Construction Industries Division
source.notes: An exact-address query returned 20 records dated 2021-2026: 11 electrical, five mechanical, three general-construction and one modular record. Project labels include VCN 1A-1B, VCN 1C-1D, VCN 2, VCN ADMIN, VLL6, later data halls, a prefabrication tent, an art project and a power box; statuses comprise 13 closed and seven issued records. Detail pages expose application-entered scope, contractor and selected inspection fields, but an IM3 project-name query returned no records and no building crosswalk, permit fee, certificate of occupancy or selected-footprint valuation was found.

research_updates.title: Water agreement supplies capacity, not use
research_updates.notes: The original and restated agreement recitals, the August 2021 water-connection agreement, Village project-status and budget records, state water-right access and public water-planning materials were reviewed. The original 303-acre property received up to 500 acre-feet per year of consumptive water rights, converted to 0.446371233 million gallons per day for the direct record. A later Tank 7 connection was budgeted at $995,000 and Greater Kudu agreed to pay all design, construction and observation costs, but neither item is a realized payment and both remain unallocated campus infrastructure. The agreement's 4.5-million-gallon worst-case delivery guarantee and 1.5-million-gallon wastewater ceiling are capacities, not use; the reported 153,000-gallon 2020 campus average could not be tied to a public meter record. Village meter histories, bills, reimbursement ledgers, connection invoices and OSE diversion records remain request targets.

source.notes: The restated agreement recites the October 4, 2016 original agreement for the 303-acre original property and its allocation of up to 500 acre-feet per year of consumptive water rights. It also states contractual peak service and wastewater limits, which are capacities rather than metered use. The added 2019 property and 2025 AI expansion are excluded.

research_updates.title: Electric utility and regulatory searches isolate no building account
research_updates.notes: PNM and NMPRC materials for the original special-service contract and cases 16-00191-UT, 18-00269-UT, 21-00031-UT, 23-00251-UT and 25-00048-UT were reviewed. The 2018 notice confirms Greater Kudu's contribution-to-production mechanism, Meta's payment guaranty and customer recovery of specified renewable PPA costs, but supplies no realized dollar amount. Public versions do not disclose an IM3-building utility identity, meter, demand, consumption, bill, payment, customer contribution in aid of construction or original-campus interconnection outlay. PNM meter histories, billing determinants, invoices, receipts and interconnection work orders remain request targets; off-site or expansion-linked renewable-project spending, landowner payments and jobs are excluded.

research_updates.title: Environmental permit is site-wide and non-operational
research_updates.notes: New Mexico Environment Department air and discharge applications, permit notices, facility and emissions registries, compliance histories and feasibility materials were searched for Greater Kudu, Project Antelope, Meta, 4250 Messenger Loop, agency interest 37303, permit 7026 and DP-1922 from 2016-2026. The 2024 air application carries forward 118 permitted stationary generators plus two temporary units for the full source and distinguishes VLL from later VCN groups, but the public copy omits the referenced plot-plan appendix and supplies no IM3 crosswalk. DP-1922 authorizes management of up to 1 million gallons per day of industrial wastewater from cooling, again at site level. Compliance tables list NOx, CO and opacity test dates from 2019-2023 without results; the state EPA-reporting layer returns no exact-name or exact-address record. Permitted counts and capacities do not prove runtime, diesel use, actual emissions, electric load, water use, discharge or environmental damages. NMED inspection reports, test results, annual emissions, excess-emission reports, metered discharge, tank and stormwater files remain request targets.

source.title: Greater Kudu LLC Air Quality Permit 7026-M6 original application
source.notes: The operating-facility application covers the full 4250 Messenger Loop source and carries forward 118 stationary emergency generators while replacing two units, plus two temporary portable units. Its unit schedule distinguishes original VLL1-VLL6 groups from later VCN groups and reports construction or installation years, but the plot-plan appendix is not included in the public copy and no group is crosswalked to IM3 record 00626785488. Compliance-history tables list required NOx, CO and opacity test dates from 2019-2023 but no test results or actual annual emissions. Potential emissions and permit limits are not runtime, fuel use, actual emissions or utility consumption.

research_updates.title: Operator, SEC and workforce sources retain payroll gaps
research_updates.notes: Meta's 2019 opening release and current factsheet, the 2021 expansion release, 2025 Form 10-K, New Mexico economic-development and Workforce Solutions reports, BLS OEWS access and current job postings were searched for headcount, occupation, wage, payroll, residence and hiring evidence. The opening release supports more than 150 campus jobs, and the current factsheet supports more than 400 operational jobs at the expanded campus; both are retained as non-additive unallocated snapshots. A 2018 state review repeats forecasts of 800-1,000 daily construction workers through 2023 and about 300 permanent jobs at full six-building operation; forecasts are not actuals. No source identifies filled selected-building headcount, direct versus contractor status, FTEs, wages, benefits, worker residence, occupations or hiring dates. The $2.5-billion current campus figure includes later expansion and is excluded; statewide or Albuquerque-area occupation wages are not substituted for Meta payroll.

source.title: Meta Platforms, Inc. 2025 Form 10-K
source.notes: The filing reports company-wide capital expenditure, headcount and global data-center properties. It does not disclose Los Lunas building-level expenditure, depreciation, operating expense, payroll, employment, suppliers, property tax, utilities or grants.

research_updates.title: Supplier and procurement searches produce identities, not payments
research_updates.notes: State economic-development reports, Village budgets, operator releases, CID permits and direct searches for Fortis, AlfaTech, APIC Solutions, Southland Industries, Cache Valley Electric, B&D Industries, Cupertino Electric and other named contractors were reviewed. Fortis identifies its role and a $2.2-billion, 3.8-million-square-foot multi-year campus program, while permit results identify additional firms; these records disclose no selected-building contract value, invoice, payment date, local purchasing share or supplier payroll. The Fortis campus total spans later expansion, and the separate $37 million PNM solar contract and renewable-project construction statistics concern off-site generation; all are excluded from selected-building supplier spending.

source.notes: The state chronology reports the first Los Lunas data-center groundbreaking in October 2016, a doubling to two buildings in July 2017, and a six-building, 330-acre campus announcement in September 2017. It does not map those buildings to IM3 record 00626785488.

research_updates.title: Community and recipient records support non-additive grants
research_updates.notes: Village newsletters and agendas, Meta grant materials and current factsheet, the 2023 PNM filing appendix, and recipient reports from United Way, Explora and named schools and nonprofits were reviewed for 2017-2026. Direct observations retain Meta's greater-than-$3.1-million cumulative Valencia County funding through June 2023, the current greater-than-$6.2-million cumulative funding disclosure, the $225,000 Wi-Fi grant, the $212,000 sum of 17 May 2023 awards and United Way's $5,000 lower-bound donor band. These company-county figures overlap and must not be summed or assigned to the selected building. Meta's November 2025 program update reports more than 210 Los Lunas-area grants and sponsorships since 2019, and a May 2026 Village quorum notice confirms another ceremony without amounts. Recipient sources generally confirmed relationships but did not disclose additional exact amounts, payment dates, restricted balances or building attribution.

source.title: Village News, May 2023
source.notes: The Village lists 17 Meta Community Action Grant recipients and an amount for each. The arithmetic sum is $212,000; it overlaps Meta's cumulative direct-funding disclosures and is not a selected-building amount.

research_updates.title: County outcomes and residual modeling remain unsupported
research_updates.notes: The direct-evidence audit ends with no residual model because no public record identifies when IM3 footprint 00626785488 opened or separates its construction and operations from the five other original campus buildings. The first building was online in 2017, the campus opened publicly in 2019, and six buildings were online by 2022, creating staggered treatment alongside other Valencia County developments and later Meta expansion. BLS QCEW county and industry files, BEA county accounts and Census workforce access were checked as potential comparison series, but they cannot identify the selected building, direct versus contractor employment, worker residence or a defensible treatment date; simultaneous county development and disclosure suppression add further limits. Without building-level capital, employment, payroll, supplier, utility and fiscal anchors, a county difference, multiplier, avoided-cost or residual estimate would manufacture precision. No synthesis fragment is created.

source.title: Village of Los Lunas FY2023 Final Budget
source.notes: The Village reports that Meta's first building went online in 2017 and six buildings were online by 2022, with two more planned. The later two-building expansion and its stated area and investment are outside the selected-building boundary.

research_updates.title: Entity, court and recorded-document searches close no payment gap
research_updates.notes: The SEC subsidiary list identifies Greater Kudu LLC as Facebook's Delaware subsidiary, aligning the entity named in Village, PNM and NMED records. Statewide New Mexico Courts business-party searches for Greater Kudu LLC and Greater Kudu from January 1, 1997 through September 6, 2026 returned zero indexed cases, while Valencia County Clerk access and exact-name recorded-document searches exposed no selected-building consideration, lien, lease payment or economic account. The court portal states that its index is not the official record, so negative results document the search trail rather than prove that no matter exists. The reported quiet-title representation found in a law-firm project list had no case number or economic amount and was not retained as evidence.

research_updates.notes: Candidate inputs were Meta's greater-than-$2.5-billion current New Mexico data-center investment, Fortis's $2.2-billion multi-year campus program and the selected footprint's 654,433 square feet. research_updates.notes: Candidate inputs were the reported 1,100-worker campus construction peak, the forecast 800-1,000 daily workers through 2023 and permit or contractor leads. Converting either count with generic durations or wages would fail observed-anchor, time-profile, geography and allocation gates. No construction model or modeled record is added.

research_updates.title: Model candidate - fiscal: ineligible
research_updates.notes: Candidate inputs were campus parcel assessed and exempt values, IRB authorization ceilings, GASB 77 schedules, generic mill rates and County Treasurer access. project_description: Meta Los Lunas is a Meta-operated data-center campus at 4250 Messenger Loop NW in Los Lunas, Valencia County, New Mexico; the selected project is the individual 654,433-square-foot IM3-mapped footprint, not the full campus. Village records say the first campus building was online in 2017, Meta's current factsheet dates the Los Lunas data center online to 2018, and Meta held the six-building program's grand opening on February 7, 2019 after an October 2016 groundbreaking. The boundary excludes later expansion buildings, off-site energy projects, tenant equipment, and other Meta facilities.
